summary: WebSocket-driven remote shell and filesystem/git/upgrade control on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent@1.0.369 connects to a configured WebSocket server and dispatches messages from that server directly into a spawned PTY on the installer's machine: `terminal_create` spawns `bash` (POSIX) or `powershell`/`cmd` (Windows) via node-pty, and `terminal_input` writes network-received bytes straight into the shell via `pty.write(msg.data)`, streaming stdout/stderr back to the server. The same WebSocket router also handles `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `git_add`, `git_commit`, `git_push`, `restart_agent`, and `upgrade_agent`; `upgrade_agent` runs `npm install <pkg>@latest` and spawns a detached bash script that stops and restarts the systemd/launchd service unit, giving the WebSocket peer arbitrary package installation and service control. Any party controlling the configured server URL — or any compromise of that server — has full-host remote code execution on every connected installer. Additionally, on startup the agent git-clones `https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git` from a mutable branch (no commit pin) into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev`, chmods hook scripts to 0755, and toggles `enabledPlugins` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, so Claude Code plugin hooks execute code that changes on every launch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
